verdict.rationale: Godot ships genuine API/CLI parity infrastructure: a documented command-line workflow for project management/export/running (godot-docs-3/12, godot-probe-4), headless mode for CI/scripted use (godot-docs-19, godot-probe-rt-1), EditorScript for running arbitrary editor actions from code (godot-docs-5/20), and EditorInterface for scripting editor window/scene/resource operations (godot-docs-22), plus a full plugin/GDExtension system to extend or replace editor tools (godot-docs-4/13/21). This shows the engine is architected so most editor functionality is reachable programmatically rather than being GUI-locked. However, evidence never explicitly confirms 1:1 parity for every UI-only feature (e.g. visual shader graphs, animation timeline editing, import wizards) via API, and there is no independent/hands-on report validating full API-equals-UI parity — only first-party docs. Missing for 10: explicit documentation or third-party confirmation that all GUI-specific editor features (visual node graphs, animation/timeline tools, import dialogs) have complete scripted equivalents, and independent corroboration of this parity claim.
